subject: phone on the toilet
title: What If You Always Scrolled Your Phone on the Toilet?

scenes.text: What if you always took your phone to the toilet? The problem isn't the germs.
In a 2025 study of one hundred twenty-five adults, sixty-six percent scrolled on the toilet, mostly news and social media.
Then time stretches. Thirty-seven percent of scrollers stayed over five minutes, versus seven percent of non-users.
About half of phone users admitted they stayed longer than they meant to.
An open toilet seat gives your pelvic floor no support, so long sitting puts pressure on the veins down there.
Scrollers had a forty-six percent higher risk of hemorrhoids, even without more straining. Your phone is a timer you can't see.

description:
What if you always scrolled on the toilet? In a 2025 PLOS ONE study of 125 adults at Beth Israel Deaconess, 66% used phones on the toilet, 37% of them stayed more than 5 minutes (vs 7% of non-users), and phone users had a 46% higher risk of hemorrhoids after adjustment.
The study shows an association, and points to sitting time rather than straining.
